subject: Post-demo speed evaluation — next steps & triage
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo speed evaluation — next steps & triage

Thanks team — quick recap from the demo with Acme this morning and suggested immediate tests. High-level takeaways:

- Acme cares about user-facing p95 latency (chat UI) and sustained tokens/sec for batch document summarization. Their current hyperscaler baseline (their measurements) shows p95 ~ 210ms and ~38 tokens/sec for their 2k-token median requests.
- Our demo numbers (default + KV cache enabled) showed p95 ~ 115ms and sustained ~68 tokens/sec on the same trace subset (see attached quicktable). p99 also looks favorable (360ms vs reported hyperscaler 540ms) but we need broader sampling.

Key open questions Acme asked we should validate before the next call:
1) Is the delta stable across larger loads and longer runs (10k–50k requests)?
2) How does quantized model performance compare to FP16 for tail latency (p95/p99)?
3) What's the sensitivity of our p95 to batch size and cold-cache vs warmed-KV cache?
4) Region/egress impact — they run heavy EU traffic; want a US->EU comparison and region-aware routing implications.

Immediate A/B test proposal (short, actionable):
- 2x 1-hour A/B runs against the same trace (50k requests each): A = Hyperscaler exported endpoint (their invited test harness), B = Redwood default runtime + KV cache.
- Collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, 95th tail CPU/GPU utilization, and error rates.
- Within B, run sub-variants: B1 = FP16 baseline, B2 = 4-bit quantized + KV cache, B3 = small-batch (batch=1) vs batched (batch=8) for long-context flows.

Ask: Jordan, can you confirm we have access/permissions to run the export harness against Acme's hyperscaler tenant? Karthik — can you own the quantized vs FP16 runs and produce a short runbook (what infra, expected costs, rough ETA)? Marissa — please prepare the one-pager for the Acme follow-up that highlights the runtimes and ops checklist.

I attached the lab scope and a quick CSV with the demo numbers. Planning to share this plan with Acme tomorrow morning unless there are objections.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo speed evaluation — next steps & triage

+1 on the plan. A couple of operational notes:
- I can get Acme the temporary test token for our test harness today — will coordinate with their eng team.
- For the hyperscaler A side, we'll need their exported trace or a proxy that mirrors their traffic (they offered to run the A side in-house and share metrics). If they don't share traces, we'll run the canonical trace they gave us in the demo.

Karthik, estimate needed infra: I think 2x VMs with 4x A100-equivalent GPUs for the 1-hour runs will cover the spike and give us stable IO. Cost estimate: ~ $1.7k per hour for both clusters combined (rough). If quant runs are cheap (4-bit), we should also record memory footprint and cold-start times.

Marissa — I'll slot a 30-min prep with you at 9:00 PT tomorrow to align the one-pager.

Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the crisp follow-up. Agree these are the right next tests. A few notes from our side:

- We can run the A side (hyperscaler) internally and share the exported metrics if that helps avoid cross-account traffic. We'll aim to produce p50/p95/p99 and raw trace IDs for the same 50k requests you propose.
- For our production profile, median token length is ~1.9k and peak is ~4k; sustained throughput target is 50–60 tokens/sec per node. p95 target for us is <200ms.

Two asks before the A/B:
1) Can you add a run that simulates cold-user flow for 1k unique sessions (to capture cold KV cache behavior)?
2) Please include a throughput step-up (20k -> 50k -> 100k requests) so we can see degradation curves.

Happy to hop on a short call Monday to align. I'll upload our internal sample traces to the drive link you provided by EOD today (I'll place them under /acme-traces).

— Samir

- Add Cold run (1k unique sessions) as a separate 30-minute step before the A/B runs.
- Throughput step-up: we'll run three ramps (20k, 50k, 100k) and capture degradation curves for p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
- Karthik to own quantized vs FP16 sub-runs and capture memory / cold-start differences.
- Jordan to coordinate the hyperscaler A-side exports (or accept their shared metrics).
- Marissa to finalize the Acme-facing one-pager + a short runbook for the next call (include acceptance criteria: p95 < 200ms, tokens/sec >= 60 sustained).

I scheduled a 30-min sync with Acme for Monday 09/06 at 10:00 PT to align on trace locations and run timings. I've created HubSpot activity (deal ACME-2026-Q3-42) and a short ticket in our lab tracker (LD-9021) to capture results.

I'll push the lab scope and checklist to the drive folder now.
